```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

The benchmark pipeline (`make benchmark`; `workflow/Snakefile`, `config/config.yaml`) prepares each dataset once, fits every method to the input it needs, and scores how well each method ranks proteins with a known change above unchanged ones: E. coli spiked into a human background in IonStar, UPS1 spiked into yeast in CPTAC. The tables and figures come from the files the pipeline exports to `inst/extdata`, so this page renders without data downloads.

- Ranking scores: fold change (`log_fc`), p-value signed by the fold change (`scaled.p_value`), t statistic (`t_statistic`)
- AUC, pAUC_5, pAUC_10: area under the ROC curve, and partial area up to a false positive rate of 0.05 or 0.1, on a 0 to 100 scale, with all contrasts of a dataset pooled
- Contrasts computed: protein and contrast pairs with a result for the ranking score, all contrasts together. Each method is scored on the pairs it computes, so pAUC_5 is plotted against this count
- Pareto front (red): the methods no other method beats on both pAUC_5 and contrasts computed
- Same pairs: a method may be on the front because it tests fewer, easier proteins. The methods that test a strict superset of its protein and contrast pairs are scored again on exactly these pairs (`same_pairs_scores()`; figure after the Pareto front, ranking by scaled p-value; `benchmark_same_pairs.tsv` has all three ranking scores)
- Level: `protein` (model fitted to protein abundances), `peptide` (model fitted to peptides, one result per protein), `protein + peptide` (hurdle: intensity on proteins, detection on peptides)
- FDP vs FDR: the false discovery proportion at each nominal FDR; a calibrated FDR lies on the diagonal
- Encoding: colour is the model family of the [prolfqua factory figure](https://github.com/fgcz/prolfqua#readme) (linear models, limma, limpa, LOD imputation, peptide level, hurdle); point shape and line type tell the models of a family apart; external tools are dark grey with open shapes. A method looks the same in every figure here and in the vignette `Score_history` (`method_scales()`, styles from prolfqua's `facade_styles.tsv`)

```{r read}
# The tables of the installed package: `make install` after `make benchmark`
extdata <- function(name, col_classes = NA) {
  path <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "prolfquabenchmark", mustWork = TRUE)
  utils::read.delim(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = col_classes)
}
scores <- extdata("benchmark_scores.tsv", col_classes = c(tool_version = "character"))
curves <- extdata("benchmark_curves.tsv")
methods <- extdata("benchmark_methods.tsv", col_classes = c(tool_version = "character"))
datasets <- extdata("benchmark_datasets.tsv")
preprocessing <- extdata("benchmark_preprocessing.tsv")
same_pairs <- extdata("benchmark_same_pairs.tsv")
```

```{r method-style}
# Colour by model family, shape and line type by model within the family: the same in every figure of both vignettes
method_style <- function(method) {
  list(
    prolfquabenchmark::method_scales(method),
    ggplot2::theme_bw(),
    ggplot2::theme(legend.key.width = grid::unit(2.5, "lines"))
  )
}
# Prints a plot from inside the results = "asis" loop, in order with the text, with its own height and caption
print_with_height <- function(plot, height, caption) {
  header <- paste0(
    "```{r, fig.height = ", height, ", fig.cap = ", paste(deparse(caption, width.cutoff = 500L), collapse = ""), "}"
  )
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(header, "print(plot)", "```"), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE))
}
```

# Methods

```{r methods, results = "asis"}
methods_url <- "https://github.com/prolfqua/prolfquabenchmark/blob/main/inst/extdata/benchmark_methods.tsv"
methods |>
  dplyr::summarise(datasets = dplyr::n(), .by = c("method", "tool", "tool_version", "level", "input", "description")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$tool != "prolfqua", .data$level, .data$method) |>
  dplyr::select("method", "tool_version", "level", "input", "datasets", "description") |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    table.attr = "class=\"table table-condensed\"",
    caption = paste0(
      "The ", dplyr::n_distinct(methods$method), " methods, with tool version, model level, the input the method ",
      "fits, the number of datasets it ran on (every dataset that provides its input, of ",
      dplyr::n_distinct(methods$dataset), ") and a short description. Per dataset and with the wall time of each ",
      "fit: <a href=\"", methods_url, "\">benchmark_methods.tsv</a>."
    )
  ) |>
  cat()
```

```{r datasets, results = "asis"}
for (dataset_name in datasets$dataset) {
  cat("\n\n# ", dataset_name, "\n\n", datasets$description[datasets$dataset == dataset_name], "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste0("- ", preprocessing$step[preprocessing$dataset == dataset_name], "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
  dataset_scores <- dplyr::filter(scores, .data$dataset == dataset_name)
  positive <- datasets$positive[datasets$dataset == dataset_name]
  negative <- datasets$negative[datasets$dataset == dataset_name]
  n_contrasts <- length(setdiff(unique(dataset_scores$contrast), "all"))
  pooled <- if (n_contrasts == 1) "one contrast" else paste("all", n_contrasts, "contrasts pooled")
  pauc_5 <- dataset_scores |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all") |>
    dplyr::select("model_name", "score", "pAUC_5", contrasts = "n_total") |>
    dplyr::mutate(method = .data$model_name)
  front <- pauc_5 |>
    dplyr::filter(prolfquabenchmark::pareto_optimal(.data$pAUC_5, .data$contrasts), .by = "score") |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$score, .data$pAUC_5)
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(pauc_5, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = contrasts, colour = method, shape = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_step(data = front, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = contrasts), direction = "vh",
                         colour = "#e34948", linewidth = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        ggplot2::aes(label = method),
        colour = "grey20",
        size = 3,
        segment.colour = "grey60",
        min.segment.length = 0,
        box.padding = 0.6,
        force = 6,
        max.overlaps = Inf,
        show.legend = FALSE,
        seed = 1
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.4))) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~score, ncol = 1) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "pAUC_5 (all contrasts pooled)", y = "contrasts computed (protein and contrast pairs)",
                    title = paste(dataset_name, "pAUC_5 vs contrasts computed")) +
      method_style(pauc_5$method),
    height = 11,
    caption = paste0(
      "Ranking accuracy against the number of contrasts computed on ", dataset_name, ". Each point is one method. ",
      "x: pAUC_5, the partial area under the ROC curve up to a false positive rate of 0.05 (0 to 100), ", pooled,
      "; the ROC curve separates ", positive, " proteins (changed) from ", negative, " proteins (unchanged). ",
      "y: contrasts computed, the protein and contrast pairs with a result. Panels rank proteins by fold change (log_fc), ",
      "by p-value signed by the fold change (scaled.p_value) and by t statistic. Colour: model family as in the ",
      "prolfqua factory figure; shape: model within its family; grey open shapes: external tools. ",
      "The red staircase is the Pareto front: ",
      "no other method has both a higher pAUC_5 and more contrasts computed."
    )
  )
  dataset_same <- dplyr::filter(same_pairs, .data$dataset == dataset_name, .data$score == "scaled.p_value")
  if (nrow(dataset_same) > 0) {
    dataset_same <- dataset_same |>
      dplyr::mutate(panel = paste0(.data$front_method, ": ", .data$contrasts, " contrasts")) |>
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$contrasts), .data$pAUC_5) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        panel = factor(.data$panel, levels = unique(.data$panel)),
        row = paste(.data$panel, .data$method, sep = "\r"),
        row = factor(.data$row, levels = unique(.data$row))
      )
    print_with_height(
      # the points of all methods first: the first layer sets the row order of each panel
      ggplot2::ggplot(dataset_same, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = row, colour = method, shape = method)) +
        ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
        ggplot2::geom_point(
          data = dplyr::filter(dataset_same, .data$method == .data$front_method),
          ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = row),
          shape = 21, size = 5.5, stroke = 1.2, colour = "#e34948", inherit.aes = FALSE
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = function(row) sub(".*\r", "", row)) +
        ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
        ggplot2::labs(x = "pAUC_5 on the front method's pairs (all contrasts pooled)", y = NULL,
                      title = paste(dataset_name, "same pairs, ranking by scaled.p_value")) +
        method_style(dataset_same$method) +
        ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none"),
      height = 1 + 0.28 * nrow(dataset_same) + 0.5 * dplyr::n_distinct(dataset_same$panel),
      caption = paste0(
        "Ranking accuracy on the same proteins on ", dataset_name, ", ranking by scaled p-value. Each panel is a ",
        "method on the Pareto front of the figure above (red circle) with the methods that test every protein and ",
        "contrast it tests and more; all are scored on the front method's pairs only (pAUC_5, ", pooled, "). A ",
        "method to the right of the red circle ranks these proteins better: the front method's position then comes ",
        "from testing fewer, easier proteins rather than from ranking them better."
      )
    )
  }
  computed <- dataset_scores |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all", .data$score == "scaled.p_value") |>
    dplyr::select(model = "model_name", `contrasts computed` = "n_total")
  dataset_scores |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all") |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c("AUC", "pAUC_10"), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
    tidyr::unite("column", "metric", "score", sep = " / ") |>
    dplyr::select(model = "model_name", "level", "column", "value") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "column", values_from = "value", names_sort = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::left_join(computed, by = "model") |>
    dplyr::relocate("contrasts computed", .after = "level") |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$`pAUC_10 / scaled.p_value`)) |>
    knitr::kable(
      digits = 1,
      format = "html",
      table.attr = "class=\"table table-condensed\"",
      caption = paste0(
        "Ranking scores on ", dataset_name, ", ", pooled, ", sorted by pAUC_10 of scaled.p_value. AUC is the ",
        "area under the ROC curve and pAUC_10 the partial area up to a false positive rate of 0.1, both on a 0 to ",
        "100 scale, for ranking by fold change, scaled p-value and t statistic. Contrasts computed: protein and ",
        "contrast pairs with a p-value."
      )
    ) |>
    cat()
  dataset_curves <- dplyr::filter(curves, .data$dataset == dataset_name)
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(dplyr::filter(dataset_curves, .data$curve == "ROC"),
                    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = method, linetype = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_step() +
      ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.2)) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~score) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "false positive rate", y = "true positive rate", title = paste(dataset_name, "ROC")) +
      method_style(dataset_curves$method),
    height = 4.5,
    caption = paste0(
      "ROC curves on ", dataset_name, ", ", pooled, ". y: fraction of ", positive, " proteins (changed) ranked ",
      "above a threshold, the true positive rate; x: fraction of ", negative, " proteins (unchanged) above it, ",
      "the false positive rate, shown up to 0.2. One curve per method; panels rank by fold change, scaled ",
      "p-value and t statistic. Colour: model family as in the prolfqua factory figure; line type: model within its ",
      "family; grey: external tools."
    )
  )
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(dplyr::filter(dataset_curves, .data$curve == "FDP"),
                    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = method, linetype = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
      ggplot2::geom_step() +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "nominal FDR", y = "false discovery proportion", title = paste(dataset_name, "FDP vs FDR")) +
      method_style(dataset_curves$method),
    height = 4.5,
    caption = paste0(
      "Calibration of the FDR each method reports on ", dataset_name, ", ", pooled, ". x: nominal FDR threshold; ",
      "y: fraction of ", negative, " proteins (unchanged) among the proteins called significant at that ",
      "threshold, the false discovery proportion. One curve per method, colours and line types as in the ROC figure. A ",
      "calibrated FDR lies on the grey diagonal; curves above it are anti-conservative, with more false ",
      "discoveries than the FDR promises."
    )
  )
}
```
